$description: Canonical elevation source. Hand-edit this file only; dist/ is generated.

meta.note: Six levels, measured across ALL FOUR content artboards. The first pass swept only D5-0 and missed both `hairline` (the most-used level of all) and `overlay`. Each level that carries a drop shadow is a Tailwind shadow with a 1px hairline ring in front of it. The ring is the part that carries the system's look: surfaces are defined by a crisp edge, with the drop doing very little.
meta.themeVarying: hairline, card and overlay flip their ring between themes - near-black in light, near-white in dark, because a dark surface needs a light edge to read as raised. thumb and raised do not vary.

none.usage: Inputs, textareas and other controls that sit flush in a surface. The reference gives these no shadow at all - they are distinguished by their fill, not by lift.

hairline.usage: A 1px ring in the border colour with no drop at all - the most-used elevation in the system (~50 occurrences across both themes). Use it wherever an element needs an edge but no lift: swatch tiles, chart cells, bordered grid items. It is a border that costs no layout, which is why it is a shadow and not a border.

card.usage: Every card and panel. Its ring is a near-black/near-white alpha rather than the solid border colour `hairline` uses.

thumb.usage: The knob of a switch, and the active tab in a tab track. Same drops as card, with no ring - it sits on a coloured or filled track, where a hairline would read as a seam.

raised.usage: Slider thumbs. An element that floats just off the surface it controls. Its ring does not vary by theme.

overlay.usage: Anything that floats above the page: chart tooltips in the reference, and by extension dropdown panels, popovers, menus and date pickers. Pairs with radius-14, which is what the reference's tooltip uses - NOT radius-24, which is for cards.

notes.ringVsBorder: Every ring here is part of the shadow, not a CSS border. That keeps it outside the box model, so it never shifts layout. Do not reimplement as a border unless the platform forces you to - Compose does.
notes.tailwindBase: card and thumb use Tailwind's shadow-sm drops; raised uses shadow-md; overlay uses shadow-lg. Exactly, in each case.
notes.avatarRing: Overlapping avatars in the reference use a 2px ring in the page colour (#FFFFFF light) to separate them. That is the same idea as ring-offset rather than an elevation, so it is not a token here - draw it with ring-offset at 2px.
